A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MANTRA and provide readable main text, mathematics, figures, tables and appendices. Renamed models and reorganized results can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original nine-model benchmarking on topological prediction tasks, including barycentric-subdivision evaluations, in Section 3 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional model evaluations in Section 3 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The proposed dataset construction, feature-generation procedures and task losses remain unchanged. Additional architectures are existing comparison methods; expanded model explanations and renamed connectivity indices do not establish a revised proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 Table 10 extends reported orientability evaluation to three-dimensional manifolds; v1 reports this task only for surfaces. The dataset tables otherwise describe the same collections. The revised total of 250,359 three-manifolds matches v1 Table 1 and does not establish added data.

E2.justification: The comparison expands from nine to twelve models by adding CellMP, CT and DECT, substantially broadening architectural coverage. TransfConv is renamed UniMP, retaining the same cited method. CT and CellMP participate in subdivision comparisons; DECT is explicitly excluded.

E3.justification: v2 additionally reports accuracy for orientability and homeomorphism prediction and introduces configurations for the added comparators, including CT positional encoding. The existing six-epoch budget, learning rate, Adam optimizer and stratified 60/20/20 splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing feature-initialization and single-subdivision robustness analyses extend to additional models, including remeshing tests for CT and CellMP. v1's dedicated family-by-initialization summary in Table 8 disappears, although per-feature results and their discussion remain.

E5.justification: Detailed tables switch from mean and standard deviation accompanied by a best-run maximum to mean and standard deviation alone. Both versions report five runs. v2 also explicitly clarifies that Table 2 summarizes best-run performances across model configurations rather than uncertainty across seeds.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for three comparators, three-manifold orientability and additional accuracy metrics, while revising existing three-manifold scores and timings. For example, SCN degree-input beta0 accuracy changes from 0.38 ± 0.35 in v1 Table 21 to 0.95 ± 0.06 in v2 Table 9. Table 6 also corrects doubled surface homeomorphism counts.

T1.justification: Appendix A's definitions and derivations remain unchanged, but Section 2 adds the stronger assertion that every complete graph with n > 7 triangulates both orientable and nonorientable surfaces. This unqualified mathematical claim conflicts with Appendix A.4's constraint 3t = 2e: for n = 8, it would require 56/3 triangles.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement and conclusion retain the central claims: MANTRA supplies a large, diverse, intrinsically higher-order benchmark; higher-order models generally outperform graph models but struggle with topological prediction and subdivision invariance. Additional comparisons principally change the supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning small triangulations, dimensional coverage and missing real-world geometry. It replaces v1's auxiliary-task hypothesis about the beta2–orientability gap with an interpretation of similar performance, qualifies subdivision degradation by above-random performance, and discusses DECT's invariance and persistent-homology/MAPPER alternatives.

D1.justification: New Appendix B documents JSON examples, required fields, legacy-format conversion and storage choices; Appendix D supplies hyperparameters for the added models. Named repository addresses and explicit Zenodo DOIs replace anonymous links and promised archival availability. The previously stated GAT head count is omitted.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially expands positioning against existing higher-order network and neuroscience datasets, including Benson, Giusti and Tadic, qualifying the earlier Torus-only assertion to purely higher-order data. Additional discussion connects MANTRA to prior Betti-number prediction, graph-benchmark critiques, persistent homology and MAPPER.

P1.justification: v2 adds substantial dataset-design and model explanations, reorganizes the appendices and groups results by task. Reproducibility material moves into Section 2, while introduction and interpretation passages are rewritten. Some edits introduce incomplete sentences in Sections 3.1–3.2.

P2.justification: Fourteen detailed result tables become four consolidated task tables, replacing rotated Betti tables with upright displays and adding accuracy columns. Figure 1 is redrawn in color, dataset-field and hyperparameter lists become tables, and the throughput table is transposed.

improvement.justification: Broader comparator coverage, corrected dataset counts, practical access documentation and explicit transferability limits improve the benchmark's usefulness. These gains are moderated by the unchanged six-epoch training and acknowledged tuning limitations, plus new mathematical and prose errors, including Section 2's unrestricted complete-graph assertion.
